cards.title: Teacup Weather Window Helper
cards.tableFit: 15-minute cooperative, screen-free printable family-table card for younger writers who can add one tiny setting clue and one helper choice.
cards.adultSetup: Print one card per writer, place pencils in the middle, and model one short setting detail before the table writes.
cards.kidDirection: Choose a teacup weather clue, pick the helper at the window, and write what the helper notices first.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask the table which tiny weather clue is easiest to picture, then invite each writer to choose a helpful character.

pageSections.heading: Window Weather
lines: The teacup window shows weather shaped like ____________________.
The tiny room smells like ____________________ when the weather changes.
The sill holds a small clue: ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Helper Choice
lines: The helper at the window is ____________________.
The helper decides to check ____________________ first.

pageSections.heading: Story Start
lines: First, the weather clue moves toward ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Table talk: One setting detail I can add for the family table is ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The helper looks through the window and sees ____________________.
cards.roundWrapLine: Round wrap: The detail that made our teacup scene clearer was ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Point to a favorite line, then write one more window clue: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story: At home, add a new weather clue that changes ____________________.

cards.title: Spoon Ferry Harbor Cargo Note
cards.tableFit: 16-minute cooperative, screen-free printable family-table card for writing a clear ferry sequence with one sound, color, or texture.
cards.adultSetup: Print the card, set out pencils, and place a simple paper harbor path in the middle for writers to point at while planning.
cards.kidDirection: Send the spoon ferry across the lunchbox harbor, choose its cargo, and write three calm story steps.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask writers to name one harbor detail they can hear, see, or feel before they write the ferry note.

pageSections.heading: Harbor Setting
lines: The dock color I picture is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Cargo Choice
lines: The careful paper route goes around ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Table talk: The sensory detail I can offer the table is ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The spoon ferry carries ____________________ across the harbor.
cards.roundWrapLine: Round wrap: The step that helped our ferry story move forward was ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Trace the ferry path silently, then write one cargo clue: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story: At home, add one more harbor sound or color: ____________________.

cards.title: Pocket Park Notice Board Helper
cards.tableFit: 15-minute cooperative, screen-free printable family-table card for inventing one useful notice and one friendly spoken line.
cards.adultSetup: Print the card, offer pencils and blank paper strips, and remind writers that every notice is invented for the story world.
cards.kidDirection: Create a pocket park notice, choose the helper who reads it, and write what the helper says.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask the table what kind of small park job a helper could do, then invite one short spoken sentence.

pageSections.heading: Notice Board
lines: The pocket park notice asks for ____________________.
The board has a small drawing of ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Park Helper
lines: The helper who reads the notice is ____________________.
The helper chooses this job because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Spoken Line
lines: The helper says, "I can help with ____________________."

cards.tableTalkLine: Table talk: A helpful notice idea for our park is ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The pocket park helper says, "____________________."
cards.roundWrapLine: Round wrap: The spoken line that made our park helper clearer was ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Skip reading aloud and copy one notice line here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story: At home, add one new pocket park notice about ____________________.

cards.title: Button Bakery Map Fix
cards.tableFit: 17-minute cooperative, screen-free printable family-table card for replacing one vague map clue with a clearer bakery detail.
cards.adultSetup: Print the card, set out pencils, and offer beside, past, near, and around as gentle direction words.
cards.kidDirection: Fix the bakery map by choosing one mixed-up clue, adding a direction word, and writing the clearer route.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask writers to point to one bakery object on the card and make the route more specific before the round wraps.

pageSections.heading: Clearer Clue
lines: I can replace a vague word with ____________________.
The bakery detail that helps readers is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Fixed Route
lines: First, follow the crumb path beside ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Table talk: The clearer direction I can add is ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The button baker fixes the map by changing ____________________.
cards.roundWrapLine: Round wrap: The revision that made our route easier to follow was ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Draw one arrow first, then write the clearer clue: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story: At home, revise one bakery map clue into ____________________.

cards.title: Penny Path Compass Shop Ending
cards.tableFit: 16-minute cooperative, screen-free printable family-table card for choosing a gentle ending and adding one compass-shop line of dialogue.
cards.adultSetup: Print the card, place pencils nearby, and invite writers to choose a calm ending that finishes the route on paper.
cards.kidDirection: Follow the penny compass, choose where the route ends, and write what the shop helper says there.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask the table which ending feels complete, then have each writer add one short shop-helper sentence.

pageSections.heading: Compass Setting
lines: The path under the counter looks like ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Shop Helper
lines: The helper says, "This path leads to ____________________."

pageSections.heading: Ending Choice
lines: The route could end with a discovered object: ____________________.
The route could end with a helpful note: ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Table talk: The ending choice I can offer the family table is ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: At the compass shop, the helper says, "____________________."
cards.roundWrapLine: Round wrap: The ending that made our Penny Path story feel complete was ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Choose the ending silently, then write one compass clue: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story: At home, add one more ending detail about ____________________.
